cultivar: Cultivars tested in Yizheng include Baiye 1, local population plants, Huangjinya, Longjing Changye and Fuding Dahao
processing: Typical of slim spring greens: young shoots are fixed by heat, straightened and shaped, then dried.
harvest_season: Spring, as with other Jiangsu greens.
appearance_dry: Long, slim, bright green strands, compared to new willow shoots.
appearance_liquor: Clear and bright, a pale green-yellow.
taste_profile: An elegant, high aroma and a fresh, mellow taste.

brewing.notes: These are usual settings for a slim spring green. A glass lets you watch the strands, and cooler water protects the sweetness.

vintage_note: Sold as a spring green. As with other Jiangsu greens, it is best within a year and is not aged.
description:
Lüyang Chun is a modern green tea from the low hills west of Yangzhou, with Yizheng and its Nashan area at the centre. The name means green-willow spring, and the long slim leaf really does look like a new willow shoot.

Like other slim spring greens, it is typically fixed by heat, straightened and dried. A local study comparing five cultivars grown in Yizheng ranked Baiye 1 best suited to this style, ahead of population plants, Huangjinya and Longjing Changye, with Fuding Dahao last. So the plant behind your bag matters.

The cup is clear and fresh, with a refined aroma and a mellow finish. Treat it gently: water around 80 °C and an open vessel, as with other slim spring greens.

It is mostly a regional tea. Check for the Yizheng origin and the year, and buy the freshest spring lot you can.
history: Lüyang Chun dates from 1991, so it is young, though it draws on an older local story: tea from the Yangzhou area is traced to the Tang and Song, its tea was listed as tribute under the Song, and the Shugang hills on the edge of the city are themselves said to take their fame from tea.
